ops.body:
# cc-pool v0.21-native redesign (v3): ownership fencing, upgrade migration, pool, observation lane

Inputs: verdict note efa8ce2 (daemonkit store; its measurement section stands), mechanical-lane note 0f6686e (branch dk-v021-migration @ bf52839, worktree /private/tmp/w5-cc-pool), the v2 adversarial review round (sol security refuter + opus convention reviewer; consolidated verdict accepted in full), and the round-2 verify pass over v2 (sol; four findings — two blockers, one major, one minor — all accepted with their decisions bound and folded below; v1 and v2 are preserved in this note's history). One type correction made while folding round 2: the verdict's "default Trust.Control to daemonkit.ServingSameUser()" cannot be written — ServingSameUser() is Serving-typed (daemonkit serving.go:38) and Trust.Control is *Requirement (daemon.go:167) — so the same-user control posture is spelled Control: nil, the floor alone; substance identical (§A). And one line correction to the verdict's own finding-4 parenthetical: the receipt struct is account_mutation.go:124-158 (Owner :147), while :181-197 is BeginAccountMutationRequest (Owner :196) — the real lines are folded. Owner decision, verbatim: "change cc-pool to the new design, dont try to port bad old design." All cites verified against cc-pool origin/main 8df819e, daemonkit v0.21.3 (docs/DESIGN.md, docs/MIGRATING-0.21.md, ci/exported.txt), daemonkit v0.20.9 (module cache), fusekit@b313adf (pinned — fusekit main has since moved to ab2b9d3, where catalogservice/handles.go no longer exists), synckit v0.37.1.

## A. Ownership + fencing successor

### The old fence, as verified

- Fence value: CredentialOperationFence{Token, Owner proc.Record, Epoch uint64} (internal/store/credential_operation.go:282). Every fenced write is a SQL CAS on (token, owner_record, owner_epoch): StageCredentialOperationPublication (:831-835), settleCredentialOperation's DELETE (:1052-1056), advanceCredentialOperation (:1739-1748), AbandonPreparedCredentialOperation (:1199-1202); pending_adds equally in ReleaseAccountIndex/consumeReservation (internal/store/reserve.go:70, :89) and PendingAddReservationsOwnedBy (:328-343); account_mutations mirror it (internal/store/account_mutation.go).
- owner_record BLOBs live in FIVE tables (store.go:61, :91, :134, :233, :283) — the two receipt tables included: account_mutation_receipts (store.go:106) and credential_operation_receipts (:268) persist owner_record too, and receipts are not inert history — CredentialOperationEvidence reads them on the evidence path (store/credential_operation.go:666) and settleCredentialWrite replays their publication payloads (pool/credential_operation.go:870).
- owner_record bytes = json.Marshal(proc.Record) (encodeCredentialOwner :2707; the 18-field struct at daemonkit@v0.20.9/proc/reaper.go:58-94); equality is canonical-bytes equality (sameCredentialOwner :2736), in Go and in SQL. Decodes happen on scan for actives AND receipts: scanCredentialOperation (:1816, decode at :1846), the receipt scanner (:1948), reserve.go:411, and account_mutation.go's mirror sites.
- Owner mint: pool.Manager.credentialOwnerRecord (internal/pool/manager.go:24) = proc.CurrentIdentity() + reaper.TrackIdentity(..., CredentialOwnerRecoveryID) (internal/pool/workers.go:74, :27) — the daemon tracks ITS OWN identity in the worker FileStore so a successor's reaper can mint a durable ReapReceipt for it.
- Takeover: TakeoverCredentialOperation (:1074) requires verifyProcessRetirement (:1139-1160): a valid proc.ReapReceipt whose Record equals the dead owner and whose ReaperGeneration equals the new owner's generation, verified by the reaper — then the epoch CAS: SET owner_record=new, owner_epoch=owner_epoch+1 WHERE token=? AND owner_record=old AND owner_epoch=? (:1113-1119).
- Recovery driver: the receipt feed (internal/pool/credential_recovery.go:26 RecoverRetiredCredentialOwners, called at daemon boot from startProductRuntime, internal/daemon/transport.go:230): page ReapReceipts per CredentialOwnerRecoveryID; per receipt take over / settle every row OwnedBy(receipt.Record); AcknowledgeReap only when zero rows remain (:180-200). The un-acked receipt is the durable cross-crash work list.

### The successor

New owner identity, cc-pool-owned — internal/store/owner.go (new file):

```go
type OwnerRecord []byte // canonical bytes; the SQL equality key, opaque once stored

type ownerIdentity struct {
    V       int    `json:"v"`       // 2 — no proc.Record era ever wrote this
    PID     int    `json:"pid"`     // diagnostic
    Started int64  `json:"started"` // unixnano, diagnostic
    Nonce   string `json:"nonce"`   // 16 random bytes hex — the identity
}

func MintOwnerRecord(now time.Time) (OwnerRecord, error) // json.Marshal(ownerIdentity{...}); deterministic (fixed struct, declaration order)
func (o OwnerRecord) Validate() error                    // non-empty, <= 1 KiB
```

- Minted once per daemon generation inside Start; pool.Manager holds it as a field (Manager.owner OwnerRecord), replacing credentialOwnerRecord()/MutationOwner()'s per-call proc.CurrentIdentity (manager.go:24, :43). No persistence: after a crash nobody needs the old bytes decodable, only comparable.
- The owner-mint gate survives the retype, restated because A.1 rests on it: manager.go:25/:44's error-returning mints ("credential mutation requires exact worker authority" / "requires daemon worker ownership") become a field, so enforcement moves to the entries — a zero-value or invalid OwnerRecord is refused at every Begin*/Reserve entry via OwnerRecord.Validate, retained exactly where proc.Record.Validate sits today: ReserveAccountIndex (reserve.go:31), PendingAddReservationsOwnedBy (:332), BeginCredentialOperationRequest validation (:506 path), and the account-mutation Begin validation (validateAccountMutationRequest, account_mutation.go:1635-1643 — the Owner.Validate at :1641).
- Store retypes — actives AND receipts (the receipt omission was a review blocker): CredentialOperationFence.Owner, CredentialOperation.Owner (:289), CredentialOperationReceipt.Owner (:338), PendingAccountReservation.Owner, the account-mutation owners (account_mutation.go:81, :108, and the receipt owner :147 — the receipt struct is :124-158), BeginCredentialOperationRequest.Owner (:367), BeginAccountMutationRequest (account_mutation.go:181-197, its Owner at :196), ReserveAccountIndex(owner) (reserve.go:30) all become OwnerRecord. sameCredentialOwner becomes bytes.Equal; encodeCredentialOwner/mustEncodeCredentialOwner/decodeCredentialOwner (:2707-2740) delete; every scanner raw-scans the column bytes without decoding (active :1846, receipt :1948, reserve.go:411, account_mutation.go's decode sites) and every insert raw-inserts (json.Marshal at account_mutation.go:278 becomes the bytes themselves); every receipt validator/equality check flips to byte equality. Comparison sites, extrapolated in full: pool/credential_operation.go:130's `boundary.operation.Owner != owner` becomes !bytes.Equal, and so do its siblings requireCurrentAccountMutationOwner (internal/daemon/account_mutation.go:963-971, the `mutation.Owner != owner` at :968) and currentAccountMutationOwner (:956-961); the accountMutationOwner test seam at internal/daemon/server.go:163 retypes to func() (store.OwnerRecord, error).
- Every SQL CAS site is unchanged: same columns, same WHERE, same epoch bump.

Retirement proof moves from a verified receipt to Serve's flock:

- Delete: ProcessRetirementVerifier (:20), verifyProcessRetirement (:1139), the receipt+verifier parameters of TakeoverCredentialOperation (:1074) and its account-mutation sibling, CredentialOwnerRecoveryID, TrackIdentity, the reaper/FileStore plumbing in workers.go, the receipt-driven RecoverRetiredCredentialOwners machinery (credential_recovery.go), and TakeoverRetiredAccountMutationPage's receipt scan (pool/credential_recovery.go:207-210).
- Replace with a claim pass in Start: pool.Manager.ClaimForeignLanes(ctx) (internal/pool/credential_recovery.go rewritten; not "Adopt" — adoption is already taken twice, by internal/daemon/adoption.go's credential-rotation adoption / Manager.AdoptRotatedToken (usage.go:320) and by daemonkit's Ctx.Adopt pid takeover): page three new store queries — CredentialOperationsNotOwnedBy(self, afterAccountID, limit), AccountMutationsNotOwnedBy, PendingAddReservationsNotOwnedBy (foreign = owner_record <> my bytes; the WHERE flips from owner_record=?) — and per row run the domain logic recoverCredentialOperation keeps (pool/credential_operation.go:1465-1504, minus the receipt parameter): account-identity re-check, TakeoverCredentialOperation(fence-from-row, self) where fence.Owner is the row's opaque bytes echoed into the CAS, then abandon prepared no-I/O lanes / resume the rest. Pending adds keep the RetirePendingAdd proof hook. Wire it exactly where the old recovery ran: the new Start, before the scheduler and before business admission opens (ready = Start returned; today transport.go:212-245).

### Two-owner exclusion — the takeover walk, old vs new

Old: (1) A owns rows; (2) A dies; (3) B's reaper probes A's tracked identity, observes absence, mints durable ReapReceipt{Record: A}; (4) B verifies the receipt and CASes each row's epoch A→B; (5) a straggler write under A's fence hits rows-affected=0 → ErrCredentialOperationOwner; (6) the receipt is acked only when zero A-owned rows remain, so a crash mid-recovery re-presents the work.

New, step by step:
1. Only the daemon process writes owner-keyed rows. Today every Begin* owner comes from Manager.credentialOwnerRecord, daemon-gated (manager.go:25, :44); post-change the gate is Validate-at-entry (above); the synckit-helper runtime never mints one (workers.go:119 OpenHostSyncHelperOwners has no TrackIdentity, and its successor is synckit v0.37's Prepare(daemonkit.Ctx) hook); scripts/sync-sim/seed fabricates owners for simulation only. A verification step asserts this stays true.
2. At most one daemon process exists per label — within v0.21-only generations: daemonkit.Serve step 2's inode flock, acquired before recovery and Start, ErrBusy on a live incumbent, no takeover verb (daemonkit docs/DESIGN.md §5.1). The flock is released only when drain fully settles; a wedged drain lands stages in Drained.Abandoned, deliberately retains the flock, and launchd's ExitTimeOut SIGKILLs — the successor cannot acquire until the incumbent PROCESS is gone. The one window this flock cannot see — a live v0.20.9 incumbent at the flag day, which holds a DIFFERENT lock — is closed by §B's cross-era gate.
3. Therefore when the successor's Start runs, every foreign-owned row's owner is either a dead process or a fully drained one — and cc-pool's Product.Drain (D) stops the scheduler and joins the saga WaitGroup (internal/daemon/server.go's s.wg) before returning, so "fully drained" means no saga goroutine remains.
4. The epoch CAS is unchanged and stays the belt for the impossible straggler: any write under a superseded fence still fails on rows-affected=0.
5. Crash mid-claim: the claim is a per-row CAS; un-claimed rows stay foreign and the next Start's scan re-presents them. The durable work list is the rows themselves — strictly stronger than the receipt feed, which could name owners whose rows were already settled.
6. Begin-time protection is preserved: BeginCredentialOperation still refuses a foreign-owned lane with ErrCredentialOperationRecoveryRequired (:420, :441, :546 semantics; the comparison is now bytes-vs-self), and executeCredentialOperation's wait/retry arms (pool/credential_operation.go:348-401) keep handling it.

Deliberately NOT rebuilt: a durable acknowledgeable reap-receipt feed. Once rows are the work list nothing consumes receipts; per daemonkit DESIGN.md §6, "the record's absence asserts what a receipt asserted." If a future consumer needs reap durability rows cannot express, cc-pool owns that persistence via daemonkit/durable then — not now.

### The second durable owner identity: credential_locks

internal/pool/credential_locks.go carries its own serialized proc.Record — the journal/marker `Worker proc.Record` JSON fields (:61, :69) — and gets the same opaque-bytes treatment as the store owners:

- The Worker field becomes the same v2 OwnerRecord bytes the Manager minted. The record is written-and-echoed identity, never probed for liveness (no probe site exists in the file; the 32-hex nonce stays the real per-lease identity), so opaque bytes lose nothing.
- The mint currentCredentialLockWorker (:483-499 — proc.CurrentIdentity + proc.ProcessGeneration + CredentialOwnerRecoveryID) deletes with CredentialOwnerRecoveryID; validateCredentialLockJournal's kind checks (:606-609 — Worker.Validate, RecoveryID equality, ProcessGroup) collapse to OwnerRecord.Validate; the marker↔journal equality (:640 `marker.Worker != journal.Worker`) becomes bytes.Equal.
- The guard flock (:112-114, proc.FileLockSpec{Path: journalPath + ".guard", Mode: FileLockExclusive, Deadline: credentialCASWorkerTimeout}) becomes durable.AcquireLock with the same derived deadline; any consumer-facing sentinel is aliased (`= durable.ErrLockBusy`), never re-errors.New'd — sentinel identity is load-bearing across the fleet.
- The daemonstate writes (daemonstate.WriteFileDurable/SyncDir at :196, :347, :359, :409, :524, :543, :551) become durable.WriteFile/durable.SyncDir per MIGRATING §5.

### Daemon identity and boot, where ownership starts

- internal/daemon/spec.go (new): one `func Spec(program daemonkit.Program, control *daemonkit.Requirement) daemonkit.Daemon` — the control requirement stays a PARAMETER per fusekit@b313adf holder/trust.go:34 (runtimeTrust reads config.Trust.Controller; holder/runtime_test.go:1149 injects testProcessRequirement), but after round 2 the parameter is a test seam only: EVERY real call site passes nil. The posture, stated honestly (a round-2 major): Trust.Control is enforced at control attachment (daemonkit internal/wire/server.go:250-255; daemon.go:167 — "Gates Control and the wire Drain verb") and WaitReady itself routes through Control (waitready.go:71-77), so under ANY non-nil Control, Health/Ensure/WaitReady/Drain are gated exactly as hard as Control — "floor-only Health" and a signed production Control cannot both be true, which v2 claimed. The real health/control callers are all same-user and mostly unsigned: internal/cli/service.go's status/stop/uninstall lane (observeDaemonRuntime :35, runServiceUninstall :176, stopDaemonService :234, daemonHealth :424 — the Homebrew-installed CLI Mach-O), the statusapp hooks stop path (hooks.go:123, :127 — the signed widget, which passes a same-user check trivially), and the .test suite. Decision folded: Trust.Control defaults to the same-user posture under the owner's CLI-daemon waiver — spelled Control: nil, the floor alone (daemon.go:167; the same-EUID floor runs unconditionally on both ends before Trust is consulted, :163-165), the one type-correct spelling since ServingSameUser() is Serving-typed (serving.go:38) and cannot sit in the *Requirement field. v2's production arm — &daemonkit.Requirement{TeamID: ServiceTeamID, SigningIdentifier: ServiceRoleID} — is withdrawn; the Stop/Receipt/Readiness role table (transport.go:196-209) dissolves into the same-user floor with no signed successor, matching today's unprotected lane (transport.go:200 AllowUnprotected: true; client attach Role: trust.UnprotectedRole, client.go:967; daemon_test_server_test.go:100-101). The rest of Spec: Label "com.yasyf.cc-pool" (protocol.go:24 ServiceRoleID); Program daemonkit.Stable() (the stable exec path TCC grants key on — memory 1d978f2; today's plist runs the brew Mach-O via ccpAgent, internal/cli/service.go:61-75); Schemas from wirebuildgen (D); Restart: daemonkit.RestartAlways stated explicitly (fusekit@b313adf holder/runtime.go:163 precedent — see traps); Shutdown/Handshake/MaxFrame stated from current values (daemonShutdownTimeout, the retired ladder's ceilings); Concurrency stated with its arithmetic in §D; Trust{Serving: daemonkit.ServingSameUser() (a Homebrew tool — the named waiver, stated), Control: nil via the parameter (the same waiver on the control lane), Business: nil (successor of AllowUnprotected: true)}.
- internal/cli/service.go: install/uninstall/status rebuild on daemonkit.Open(Spec) + Ensure/Control; ccpAgent, daemonServiceControllerConfig (:88), the plist adaptation + Homebrew-formula service-block lockstep (cc-pool doc 3762436) retire — Ensure owns the plist. The evict machinery deletes with it: evictTimeout (internal/daemon/server.go:70-71, set at :181) and its ListenerWait consumption (transport.go:96) have no v0.21 successor — Serve's flock refuses a live incumbent with ErrBusy (DESIGN.md §5.1); no wait-for-eviction exists. (v1 named SingleEntrant and peer.go here; neither exists in cc-pool — the deletion scope is exactly the evictTimeout/ListenerWait machinery above.)
- The statusapp/hooks residual the mechanical lane froze: internal/statusapp/hooks.go:123,127 stop path → daemonkit Open(Spec) → Control(ctx) → Drain (roles dissolve into the Control lane). The holderbridge deployment_identity roles residual is now §E's delete decision — v1's cc-pool-local PolicyRole retype ("SAME serialized values") is withdrawn there.
- internal/store/store.go:28, :444-446 lifecycleLock (proc.FileLockShared): delete. The mechanical lane measured that nothing takes the exclusive side; a shared lock with no exclusive writer guards nothing. SQLite's own locking remains the store's concurrency control. The read-only Lstat probe (:440) goes with it.

## B. Upgrade story for live data — gate, then adopt; never migrate

Decision: compat-free opaque-bytes claiming — the upgrade IS the crash-takeover path — behind a one-cycle cross-era gate. No one-time row rewrite, no compat read path, no quiesce step.

### The flag-day gate (v0.21.x only, deleted in v0.22)

The v0.21 flock cannot exclude a v0.20.9 incumbent, and the stated "Ensure drains the old daemon" does not hold unassisted — this was a review blocker:

- A pre-cut daemon refuses a protocol-2 peer outright — proven against a live listener for v0.20.10 (daemonkit ci/mixedera/mixedera_test.go:184, "refuse/cut-client-precut-daemon", where precutBoundary = "v0.20.10" per mixedera_test.go:74-75), and v0.20.9 speaks protocol 1 (daemonkit@v0.20.9/wire/frame.go:15-17, vs protocol 2 at v0.21.3 internal/wire/frame.go:12-14), so the identical refusal holds for cc-pool's pinned era — and Ensure classifies only ErrAbsent/ErrDraining as startable (ensure.go:217; classifyWire, control.go:203) — a live pre-cut incumbent surfaces as an error, not a start.
- v0.21's own exclusion cannot see it either: Serve takes the record-store lock and probes the socket, reading ECONNREFUSED as no incumbent (serve.go:173 probeIncumbent, :412). v0.20.9's exclusion is a different lock entirely: proc.FileLockSpec{Path: cfg.Socket + ".lock", Mode: FileLockExclusive} taken in listen() (daemonkit@v0.20.9/daemon/runtime.go:1086) and released only after FULL settlement — shutdown() calls lock.Close() only when product/workers/children all settled, and retains ownership otherwise (runtime.go:1153-1204 — an unsettled product retains listener and lock at :1159, lock.Close() runs only when settled at :1193-1198, and any later shortfall retains again at :1199-1204) — or on process death, when the kernel drops the flock.
- Without a gate, the two-owner window is real: a SIGTERMed-but-settling v0.20.9 daemon can cross a credential lane to applying (credentialOperationBoundary.Cross, pool/credential_operation.go:122) BEFORE its external keychain/OAuth call (applyCredentialOperation :580, the fenced MarkCredentialOperationApplied after the external work :717); the v0.21 successor claims the row; the straggler's fenced SQL loses on the epoch CAS — but the external effect already happened.

The gate, in order, at the top of the v0.21 daemon main, before daemonkit.Serve:

1. The live legacy incumbent is removed directly through launchd — NEVER through Client.Stop, whose fallback round 2 proved unreachable for exactly this case: against a live pre-cut listener, stopOnce's attach comes back as the protocol-mismatch error (stop.go:103-118 — a pre-cut daemon refuses the protocol-2 hello: proven live at v0.20.10 by mixedera_test.go:184, and v0.20.9 is protocol 1 by daemonkit@v0.20.9/wire/frame.go:15-17), the retry loop exits on !moved (stop.go:77-84), and removeAgent (:139-151) — home of the ErrNotOwned → launchd.RemoveUnmarked fallback (:144-149) — runs only after stopOnce settles, i.e. never while the old daemon lives. The one-cycle path instead calls launchd.RemoveUnmarked(ctx, runner, label) up front, before any attach — the markerless escape the v0.21.1 cut added (commit 741cc2f, first tagged v0.21.1). Exact call path: RemoveUnmarked (daemonkit launchd/apply.go:126) → removeWhen (:180-202), which reads the plist at the label's LaunchAgents path (absent → no-op success), refuses a marker-carrying plist untouched with ErrMarked (:170-171 — marked means a v0.21 install, which Remove/Client.Stop owns), and otherwise runs `launchctl bootout gui/<uid>/<label>` (:195; serviceTarget/domainTarget :455-457) then durable.Remove of the plist (:198). RemoveUnmarked is thus its own legacy detector: markerless → booted out and deleted, and the process dies — its drain settles, or launchd's ExitTimeOut SIGKILLs it; ErrMarked or no plist → no legacy incumbent, fall through to the normal flow. cc-pool supplies the ten-line exec-over-/bin/launchctl launchd.Runner (the exported type, apply.go:53; daemonkit's own runner is unexported — ensure.go:559, bound at Open, client.go:21). Uninstall leads with the same call, then routes the marked world through Client.Stop (trap 2 below).
2. Only after the bootout, blocking-acquire the legacy listener lock — exactly `pool.SocketPath() + ".lock"` = ~/.cc-pool/daemon.sock.lock (SocketPath is statePath("daemon.sock"), internal/pool/paths.go:111-114; v0.20.9 derives the lock as Socket + ".lock", runtime.go:1086) — exclusive, and HOLD it for the process lifetime. The order is load-bearing: acquired first, the lock would park forever behind a healthy incumbent nothing is killing. Acquisition is the absence proof: v0.20.9 releases that lock only after product settlement or by dying, so a successful acquire means no v0.20.9 saga goroutine exists. Holding it is the belt against a lingering v0.20.9 binary relaunching mid-cycle.
3. Only then Serve → Start → ClaimForeignLanes.

Lifespan: a one-cycle transition piece. It ships in v0.21.x and is deleted in v0.22, by which point no v0.20.9 incumbent can exist; the stale lock file becomes doctor/uninstall cleanup.

### Adopt, don't migrate — why, with evidence from the resume code

- Nothing in the resume path needs to DECODE the old owner — receipts included; it needs to (a) find foreign rows and (b) echo their owner bytes into the epoch CAS. CredentialOperationsOwnedBy / …NotOwnedBy match on bytes; TakeoverCredentialOperation's WHERE takes the bytes just read from the row (:1113-1119). The scanners' decode (:1846, :1948 → decodeCredentialOwner :2726) exists only to re-encode for comparisons — with OwnerRecord both actives and receipts read the column raw and never fail on era.
- Sequence on a real machine: gate step 1's direct launchd.RemoveUnmarked boots out the v0.20.9 daemon; the new build starts and passes gate step 2; Serve settles prior children; Start mints the v2 owner; ClaimForeignLanes pages every row whose owner_record != the v2 bytes — every old proc.Record row qualifies, byte-for-byte as stored, in the receipt tables too — CASes epoch+1 onto each active, then resumes exactly as recoverRetiredCredentialOperation does today (pool/credential_operation.go:1499-1504): prepared non-remove lanes abandon (:1199 path), applying/applied lanes settle against the keychain, account mutations re-enter their state machines, pending_adds retire via RetirePendingAdd. In-flight sagas resume, not orphan.
- The v2 encoding is deliberately un-confusable: it lacks recovery_id, so v0.20.9's Record.Validate rejects it (proc/reaper.go:99-104 requires RecoveryID), and it carries "v":2, which no proc.Record era ever wrote.

Failure modes, named:
- Crash mid-claim: per-row CAS; remaining old-format rows are still foreign at the next boot; the re-scan re-presents them. No partially-migrated state can exist because there is no migration state — only claimed rows and not-yet-claimed rows, both valid.
- Race with a not-quite-dead old daemon: excluded by the cross-era gate (above) at the flag day and by Serve's flock within v0.21 generations (A.2/A.3); belt: a v0.20.9 straggler's fenced writes CAS on (old bytes, old epoch) and lose after the claim bumps the epoch.
- Downgrade after adoption: UNSUPPORTED, stated as such — there is no recovery procedure, and none may exist. v0.20.9's decodeCredentialOwner fails loudly on v2 bytes ("credential operation owner is corrupt") in actives and receipts alike, so a downgraded daemon errors on those lanes until upgraded again. No deletion runbook: recovery deliberately quarantines an EnsureFresh/RefreshCurrent lane that died after the OAuth boundary because a single-use refresh token may already have been consumed (pool/credential_operation.go:1577-1582 — "recovery must quarantine and never retry OAuth") — the applying row IS that quarantine evidence — and receipt rows carry the exact host-sync publication payload settleCredentialWrite replays (:870). Deleting either destroys saga evidence and can double-spend a refresh token. Fleet policy is fix-forward (daemonkit DESIGN.md §8 gate 1 — v0.21.x, never a re-cut); a machine that somehow downgrades runs a loudly-broken daemon until it upgrades.
- Stale v0.20.9 stores: the old FileStore files (DisposableWorkerStorePath etc.) stop being read; daemonkit's own legacy sweep (DESIGN.md §8 gate 2) covers its bbolt, and cc-pool's leftover store files are doctor/uninstall cleanup, not load-bearing.

## C. Pool policy

Shape and caps survive; the substrate flips to Ctx:

- internal/workerexec/runner.go: Runner keeps its one method on cc-pool-owned values — Run(ctx, workerexec.CommandRequest) (workerexec.CommandResult, error); CommandRequest{Path, Dir, Args, Env, Stdin []byte, TotalTimeout} and CommandResult{Stdout, Stderr, ExitCode} mirror the v0.20.9 fields minus Receipt (daemonkit@v0.20.9/worker/pool.go:67-82) — the ~30 pass-through sites rename imports only.
- internal/pool/workers.go rewrites: workerRuntime drops pool/children/reaper/owner/claim for a Ctx-backed run surface; newProcessRuntimeAt/newWorkerRuntimeAt collapse. Scheduling is cc-pool's, per the migration guide: a Capacity-4 execution semaphore plus a QueueCapacity-4 admission bound (the chan-struct{} pair worker.Pool itself used, v0.20.9 pool.go:101-102 — about 40 lines), with cc-pool-minted sentinels workerexec.ErrCapacity / ErrTimedOut (the only fleet matcher on the old vocabulary is scripts/vm/helpers/worker-deadline/main.go:104). Caps keep their values (workers.go:16-22): MaxTotalRun 31m via context.WithTimeout inside Run; 16 MiB stdin enforced before dispatch; output caps via the ONE v0.21 field — Cmd.MaxOutput = 16 << 20 (per-stream: "caps each retained Run stream", daemonkit cmd.go:64-66), replacing the v0.20 two-field pool config (MaxStdoutBytes/MaxStderrBytes, workers.go:95-96); Cmd.MaxStdout/MaxStderr do not exist in v0.21. Behavior change, decided explicitly: v0.21 makes a shortfall an ERROR by default — ErrTruncated (cmd.go:127-133, "a silently shortened stream a caller parses is corruption"). The disposable-worker Run fails on it and propagates: stdout is a parsed encoded result, so truncation is corruption, never accepted; no accept-and-continue site exists in the worker path.
- Spawn via Ctx.Run, not OwnProcesses. Reasons: the daemon already holds Ctx from Start; Ctx.Run is exactly "one bounded disposable command, reap included" under a deadline-carrying ctx — the 31m cap's natural home; and a second OwnProcesses scope would mean a second record file whose orphans Serve's recovery does NOT settle, whereas Ctx children ride the daemon's record file and crashed generations come back as Ctx.Reclaimed before Start. Long-lived children (accountterminal PTY logins, holder session children) use Ctx.Spawn with Cmd.Session: true so the dedicated session id stays durable kill identity for the whole tree. OwnProcesses(ctx, recordPath) is for non-daemon binaries only (scripts/vm/helpers/worker-deadline, scripts/sync-sim/seed); plain os/exec where nothing needs owning.
- The synckit helper: helperruntime v0.37.1's Config{..., Prepare func(daemonkit.Ctx)} hands the helper its own Ctx — HostSyncHelperOwners (workers.go:119-137) deletes; internal/hostsync builds its Runner over that Ctx.
- The .test re-exec seam survives unchanged: the disposable worker is executable = os.Executable() resolved once at construction (workers.go:109), invoked with procscan's worker sentinel args (cmd/cc-pool/main.go:71-72 IsWorkerInvocation/RunWorker; request on stdin, result on stdout). The Runner fills Cmd{Path: executable, Args: workerArgs, Stdin: encoded request}. Under test the .test binary re-execs and TestMain's env-var branch dispatches — the fork-bomb hazard and the scripts/test.sh harness rule are untouched.

- **Cmd.Exec is mandatory — a boundary refusal, not a soft default.** §C never stated it: the zero Serving is refused at the Run/Spawn boundary, so every Ctx.Run/Ctx.Spawn site states a posture explicitly. cc-pool-wide resolution: Cmd.Exec: ServingSameUser() — the self-re-execing Homebrew Mach-O, matching §A Spec's waiver. Found by the §C lane as a test failure; applies to every lane's spawn sites including test spawns.
- **§B journal mechanism, RESOLVED (Lane A, cf7caad): era-blind carriage.** The journal/marker `worker` field became `json.RawMessage` — carried and echoed, never decoded — validated only as non-empty, compared marker↔journal by bytes.Equal on the raw value. A v0.20.9 journal decodes fine and recovers under the UNCHANGED crash-recovery path; the field was always written-and-echoed, and the recovery already trusts the guard flock for exclusion and nonce+fingerprint for target identity, so raw carriage loses nothing. Wholesale reset was rejected for a load-bearing reason: deleting the journal alone leaves the dead holder's published lock directories blocking acquisition — the roll-back has to run, and era-blind bytes let it run untouched. Handles a stale journal at ANY later acquisition, not just boot; no schema bump, no era branch. Proven by credential_locks_upgrade_test.go (literal v0.20.9 journal + published lock dir + mid-acquired marker; acquisition unblocks, residue clears).
- **§B gap, policy bound, mechanism pending Lane A:** the credential-lock journal DECODES its worker field on read (the five SQLite tables only compare bytes), so a v0.20.x crash-leftover journal fails decode and blocks acquisition post-upgrade. Bound framework: pre-v2 entries resolve by ERA DETECTION — the cross-era gate proves their holders dead — never by decoding old bytes; per-entry reclaim vs wholesale startup reset is chosen after reading what entries carry; a literal v0.20.x journal fixture test proves acquisition unblocks; credentialLockJournalSchema deliberately not bumped (a bump only relabels the failure).
